top_stories.title: Strategy (MicroStrategy) and Strive Keep Buying Bitcoin Through the Dip
points: Strategy and Strive purchased over $47 million in bitcoin opportunistically during a recent price decline.
Strategy's total holdings rose to 850,849 BTC as chairman Michael Saylor continued buying through the dip.
Large institutional purchases during downturns are historically seen as a signal of confidence in Bitcoin's long-term value.

unique_angles.point: Bank of America disclosed a $685 million position in IBIT (iShares Bitcoin Trust, an ETF that lets investors gain Bitcoin price exposure through a regular stock brokerage account), holding 14.48 million shares.

Bitcoin fell to a 12-week low near $65,000 as Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations weighed on crypto, erasing most of summer's rally; Decrypt's prediction market gives 61% odds BTC ends below $66K by Sunday and only 9% odds of topping $70,000.

items.title: Nvidia's Leadership Crisis and Make-or-Break Earnings
points: Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, its first major report since founder Jensen Huang's ouster.
Over 178,000 people, including Elon Musk, signed a petition to reinstate Huang; the Financial Times reports Huang has discussed a comeback with allies.
Trump publicly backed Huang's return, while Sam Altman expressed sympathy, noting 'heroes have flaws.'
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent countered the momentum, saying Nvidia needs a 'dramatic shake-up' and an external CEO, signaling government preference for outsider leadership.
Nvidia shares fell 4% Monday to about $156; technical charts show a potential 20% rebound if the stock clears $164.40 resistance, or a drop to $152.62 if bulls fail.
Fed minutes due Wednesday, alongside Nvidia's earnings, may firm up expectations for a December rate hike.

sections.title: Nvidia's Leadership Crisis and Earnings Showdown
points: 178,000+ people signed petition to reinstate Jensen Huang; Financial Times reports Huang discussed comeback with allies, suggesting serious interest in return.
Huang's ouster triggered intense industry backing: Elon Musk joined petition, Trump publicly backed his return, and Sam Altman sympathized while noting "heroes have flaws."
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent contradicts momentum, stating Nvidia needs "dramatic shake-up" and external CEO—suggesting government preference for outsider leadership.
Interim CEO Colette Kress leads Tuesday earnings, Nvidia's first major report without Huang; results will heavily influence investor sentiment on leadership direction.

sections.title: Nvidia Stock Technical Outlook and Market Sentiment
points: Nvidia shares fell 4% Monday to ~$156, continuing sharp decline from recent highs following Huang scandal.
Bullish scenario: if stock clears $164.40 resistance level, charts suggest potential 20% rebound is possible; bearish scenario puts $152.62 back in play if momentum fails.
Investors bracing for Tuesday earnings as a make-or-break catalyst; stock volatility reflects uncertainty over leadership and company direction.

sections.title: Bitcoin and Crypto Market Fear
points: Bitcoin dropped to 12-week low near $65,000, erasing most of summer's rally as Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations weigh on risk assets.
Decrypt Predict market assigns 61% probability that BTC trades below $66,000 by Sunday 4:59 p.m. UTC, with only 9% odds of a move above $70,000.
Two key events this week could firm expectations: Nvidia earnings Tuesday and Fed minutes Wednesday, which may signal December rate-hike likelihood.

MicroStrategy's Strategy fund bought additional Bitcoin during dip, raising total holdings to 850,849 BTC; chairman Michael Saylor commented the "dip could use a little orange" (reference to Bitcoin's color).
